summary: Re-verified the CRITICAL auth bypass fix from iteration_39 and the English-only Login page cleanup. All 4 requested items PASS. (1) POST /api/auth/google/emergent-callback with fake session_token now returns 401 (was 200 with attacker JWT) — auth bypass FIXED. (2) /login page is fully English: 0 Devanagari tokens, divider says 'or', Google button says 'Sign in with Google'. (3) 'Forgot Password?' link visible and navigates to /forgot-password. (4) Forgot Password Email flow works end-to-end: OTP sent successfully to customer@airyatra.co.in, Verify OTP screen renders with 6-digit input, resend timer, and Change Email option. Backend pytest suite: 9/10 pass (the 1 failure is a cooldown side-effect from the browser test, not a defect). The critical test 'TestGoogleEmergentCallback::test_invalid_session_rejected' now PASSES.
critical_code_review_comments: auth_routes.py lines 1826-1838: The 404 branch now correctly raises 401 with the SEC-001 comment explaining that we cannot trust client-provided data. Good defense-in-depth. Consider adding a rate limit on /api/auth/google/emergent-callback (invalid session_tokens) to slow brute-force enumeration.

GoogleLogin.js still contains ~20 Devanagari strings on the callback/redirect intermediate pages (lines 130-551). These pages appear briefly during OAuth redirect and after successful sign-in. Not blocking (login page itself is clean), but for full English-only UX these should be moved behind the language toggle as well.

success_rate.backend: 100% for requested scope (auth-bypass fix + 9/10 forgot-password suite; the 1 failure is a test-side cooldown, not a product bug)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth bypass is fully closed. If GoogleLogin.js Hindi strings on the OAuth callback page are cleaned up next, verify by navigating to /auth/google/callback with a stub session and asserting 0 Devanagari on that route. The test_forgot_password.py cooldown test should be updated to either use a fresh email per run or clear the cooldown collection in a fixture.
rca_of_the_issue: Previous iteration_39 SEC bug: on Emergent /oauth/session-data returning 404, backend accepted request.emergent_user.email and minted JWT for arbitrary email. Fix: 404 (and any non-200) now raises HTTP 401 unconditionally; JWT is only issued using verified_user from Emergent's 200 response. Confirmed via live curl: {"session_token":"invalid-xyz","emergent_user":{"email":"attacker@test.com"}} -> HTTP 401 {"detail":"Session expired or invalid. Please try logging in again."}
